ei.title: Opening Up the Web to Everyone
ei.subject: 공통영어2

fullPassage: Imagine you have fallen down and broken your right arm. There are some things that would be difficult to do with your injured arm. For example, you might not be able to carry heavy boxes or ride your bike. What about accessing the Internet? If you are right-handed, using a computer mouse or touchscreen with your left hand would be awkward and take a lot of time. However, this is a minor challenge compared to what some of us face on the Internet. For people with certain disabilities, many websites can be nearly impossible to use. This is the reason why web accessibility is important. Web accessibility is the practice of making sure that websites can be used by everyone, including people with disabilities. So what exactly makes a website accessible? Here are some common features of accessible websites. Text Descriptions of Images Along with text, most websites include other forms of information, such as images. Sometimes such visual information is important for understanding the text. This is a problem for users with visual disabilities. When they go on a website, they often use programs called “screen readers,” which read online text aloud. However, these programs cannot “read” images. Accessible websites solve this problem by providing alternative text, also known as “alt text.” Alt text is a brief description of non-textual information. For instance, if an image shows a group of students, its alt text would explain how many students are in the image and what they are doing. Screen readers can detect this alt text and read it aloud. This way, alt text ensures that people with visual disabilities can access more of the information on a website. Transcripts and Captions for Multimedia Content In some cases, audio content cannot be accessed or understood. Some people may have hearing disabilities, while others might be in places where they can’t listen to audio, such as a quiet library. Therefore, accessible websites often offer other ways to access information that is presented in audio form. For example, they may provide transcripts or captions that can help users access this information. Transcripts are text versions of the entire audio content, while captions are text versions of the audio that appear in a video as it plays. Captions include not only the text version of the spoken words but also descriptions of the music and other sounds in the video. Content That Is Easy to See and Hear Having a visual disability doesn’t necessarily mean a person can’t see at all. Some people, including many elderly people, simply have poor eyesight. This makes it difficult for them to read. For this reason, accessible websites have a background color that contrasts with the color of their text. This makes the text clear enough for most people to see. As for audio content, accessible websites allow users to adjust the volume of background sound or to turn it off altogether. This gives users both with and without hearing difficulties more control over their experience while they are using the sites. Complete Navigation Using the Keyboard Some users have disabilities that limit the movement of their hands. They rely on their keyboards, rather than a mouse, to navigate websites. On accessible websites, users can access everything on the site using only a keyboard. This means that links, buttons, and fields, which are spaces where information is entered, can be accessed through keyboard navigation. Users navigate the websites by making use of keys such as the space bar, the arrow keys, the enter key, and the tab key. For example, they can use the tab key to jump from one part of a web page to another. Both users with disabilities and those with temporarily injured hands can benefit from this kind of navigation. Indicators Other than Color That Convey Information Color blindness is a common visual disability. People with color blindness find it difficult to tell some colors apart. This can cause problems, especially when graphs and charts only use colors to show the differences between sets of information. Accessible websites use other indicators along with the colors. For example, a line in green may also be dotted, while a line in blue is solid. This ensures that everyone can tell the two lines apart. The accessibility features of websites don’t just help people with disabilities. They can make online experiences easier for everyone, regardless of abilities or situations. When websites are easy to navigate and understand, we can all benefit from a more inclusive online experience.

✅ ③ awkward(어색한)+elderly(나이 든)+solid(실선의) ← 정답

det.korean: ④ easy → awkward: 왼손으로 마우스를 쓰면 어색하고(awkward) 시간이 걸린다
det.analysis:
✅ ① broken: 팔이 부러진 상황 적절
✅ ② difficult: 하기 어려운 일들 적절
✅ ③ carry: 무거운 상자를 옮기다 적절
❌ ④ easy(쉬운) → awkward(어색한): 쉬우면 시간이 오래 걸릴 이유가 없음 ← 정답
det.tip: awkward(어색한) ↔ easy(쉬운). 뒤의 'take a lot of time'이 단서

questions.passage: Accessible websites ①<u>cause</u> this problem by providing alternative text, also known as “alt text.” Alt text is a ②<u>brief</u> description of non-textual information. det.korean: ① cause → solve: 접근성 있는 웹사이트는 이 문제를 '해결한다(solve)'
det.analysis:
❌ ① cause(일으키다) → solve(해결하다): 대체 텍스트를 제공해 문제를 해결하는 것 ← 정답
✅ ② brief: 간단한 설명 적절
✅ ③ detect: 스크린 리더가 감지하다 적절
✅ ④ ensures: 보장하다 적절
det.tip: solve the problem(문제를 해결하다) ↔ cause the problem(문제를 일으키다)

questions.passage: As for audio content, accessible websites allow users to ①<u>adjust</u> the volume of background sound or to turn it off altogether. This gives users both with and without hearing difficulties more ②<u>control</u> over their experience while they are using the sites. det.analysis:
✅ ① adjust: 음량을 조절하다 적절
✅ ② control: 더 많은 통제권 적절
❌ ③ increase(늘리다) → limit(제한하다): 장애가 손 움직임을 제한하므로 키보드에 의존함 ← 정답
✅ ④ rely: 키보드에 의존하다 적절
det.tip: limit the movement(움직임을 제한하다) ↔ increase(늘리다). 뒤의 '키보드에 의존한다'가 단서

det.tip: adjust the volume(음량을 조절하다) = change = 바꾸다, 조정하다

questions.passage: Some people, including many elderly people, simply have <u>poor</u> eyesight. This makes it difficult for them to read. For this reason, accessible websites have a background color that contrasts with the color of their text. This makes the text clear enough for most people to see.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 poor와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① cheap: 값싼, poor(가난한)의 연상 오답
✅ ② excellent: 훌륭한, 뛰어난 ← 정답(poor eyesight=나쁜 시력 ↔ excellent=좋은)
❌ ③ heavy: 무거운, 무관
❌ ④ common: 흔한, 무관
det.tip: poor eyesight(나쁜 시력) ↔ excellent(뛰어난, 훌륭한)

questions.passage: This makes the text <u>clear</u> enough for most people to see. As for audio content, accessible websites allow users to adjust the volume of background sound or to turn it off altogether. This gives users both with and without hearing difficulties more control over their experience while they are using the sites. Complete Navigation Using the Keyboard Some users have disabilities that limit the movement of their hands.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 clear와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① obvious: 분명한, clear의 동의어(함정)
❌ ② bright: 밝은, 반대가 아님
✅ ③ blurry: 흐릿한 ← 정답(clear=또렷한 ↔ blurry=흐릿한)
❌ ④ wide: 넓은, 무관
det.tip: clear(또렷한, 명확한) ↔ blurry(흐릿한). obvious(분명한)는 동의어라 오답

questions.passage:
(A) In some cases, audio <u>content</u> cannot be accessed by users with hearing disabilities. Websites add captions so that everyone can understand it.
(B) After finishing all her work for the day, she felt completely <u>content</u> and relaxed. Nothing was bothering her at that moment.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B) 두 문장에서 밑줄 친 content의 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① (A) audio content = (음성) 내용(명사), (B) felt content = 만족한(형용사) ← 정답
❌ ② (A)는 '만족한'이 아니라 '내용'
❌ ③ (A)는 '목차'가 아님
❌ ④ (B)는 '담다'가 아니라 '만족한'
det.tip: content: (A) 내용(명사, 강세 앞) / (B) 만족한(형용사, 강세 뒤)

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"a text version of the entire audio content"

det.analysis:
✅ ① transcripts: 전체 음성 콘텐츠의 텍스트 버전 = 대본 ← 정답
❌ ② captions: 자막(영상 재생 중 나타나는 부분적 텍스트)
❌ ③ indicators: 지표
❌ ④ descriptions: 설명
det.tip: transcripts=전체(entire) 음성의 텍스트 / captions=영상 속 자막. '전체'가 구별 단서

questions.passage: Users navigate the websites by __________ (make) use of keys such as the space bar, the arrow keys, the enter key, and the tab key. For example, they can use the tab key to jump from one part of a web page to another.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: 전치사 by 뒤에는 동명사(V-ing)를 쓴다. make → making. 'by making use of'는 '~을 사용함으로써'라는 뜻
det.tip: 전치사(by) + 동명사(-ing): by making use of

questions.passage: Along with text, most websites include other forms of information, such as images. Sometimes such visual information is important for __________ (understand) the text.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: 전치사 for 뒤에는 동명사(V-ing)를 쓴다. understand → understanding. 'important for understanding'은 '이해하는 데 중요한'이라는 뜻
det.tip: 전치사(for) + 동명사(-ing): important for understanding

questions.passage: As for audio content, accessible websites allow users to adjust the volume of background sound or to __________ altogether. This gives users both with and without hearing difficulties more control over their experience while they are using the sites. Complete Navigation Using the Keyboard Some users have disabilities that limit the movement of their hands. They rely on their keyboards, rather than a mouse, to navigate websites. On accessible websites, users can access everything on the site using only a keyboard.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① make it louder: 더 크게, 음량 조절과 반대 방향
❌ ② write it down: 적어두다, 문맥과 무관
✅ ③ turn it off: 끄다 ← 정답
❌ ④ speed it up: 빠르게 하다, 문맥과 무관
det.tip: '음량을 조절하거나(adjust the volume) 또는 완전히 ___' → turn it off(끄다)가 자연스러움

questions.passage: People with color blindness find it difficult to __________. This can cause problems, especially when graphs and charts only use colors to show the differences between sets of information. Accessible websites use other indicators along with the colors. For example, a line in green may also be dotted, while a line in blue is solid. This ensures that everyone can tell the two lines apart.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸에 tell some colors apart(몇몇 색을 구별하다)가 적절
det.analysis:
✅ ① tell some colors apart: 색을 구별하다 ← 정답(색맹의 특징)
❌ ② mix all the colors: 색을 섞다, 문맥과 무관
❌ ③ draw simple graphs: 그래프를 그리다, 문맥과 무관
❌ ④ read long sentences: 긴 문장을 읽다, 문맥과 무관
det.tip: color blindness(색맹) → 색을 구별하는(tell colors apart) 것을 어려워함
